title: The Secret Classroom Management Strategy Of Highly Effective Teachers
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin frames his central claim as a hidden strategy that runs in the background of the most effective teachers: deciding in advance, precisely, how every moment of classroom behavior will unfold, rather than leaving any decision to students in the moment. This doesn't mean eliminating student choice entirely — a teacher can still allow talking or design freedom — but it must be choice the teacher has explicitly authorized and taught, never a spontaneous decision students make on their own. His concrete argument is that every moment a student makes an undirected choice, teacher authority "drops like an anvil," and left unchecked, students will gradually claim more and more control over classroom conditions. The technique is deliberately individualized — how any given teacher applies it will differ — but the underlying principle stays constant: the teacher, not the class, decides how, when, and with whom things happen. He closes by arguing the payoff is relieving students of decision fatigue entirely, freeing them to focus fully on learning rather than navigating ambiguous social terrain.

quotes: It isn’t applied once and reused when needed. It isn’t a step-by-step, how-to process. I don’t believe it’s ever been revealed in the history of education.
The strategy is this: You decide beforehand how every moment will unfold in your classroom.
Every moment of student behavior/performance/action is decided by YOU.
Because every time your students choose—that is, without your express direction or instruction—your authority drops like an anvil.
The students then are relieved of the stress of decision fatigue.
